questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good academic opportunities firstly. Moreover I wanted it to be in a nice city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't get much info about my courses but everything else went smoothly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome day with an introduction to the facilities provided by Sorbonne

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Could have used a bit more info on the courses where to go what to expect etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Sorbonne provided it to me. It should be easy for master students I believe

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In the Cité Universitaire there are a lot of other exchange students so it is good for making friends with people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Kitchen was under construction for like two months :(

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Basically you send them the courses you want to take from the course catalogue and they validate it. Herafter you are on your own with finding the corses, material etc. 
I had to go to the office of the administration to confirm my enrollment and to know where to go.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a part of the administration responsible for exchange students. They answer very fast to whatever questions you may have. Very helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you are confident in your french. Else you will have a haaaard time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing courses provided. Although the execution could be improved a bit in some.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The were hard but I knew that I signed up for it.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Sorbonne provide a lot more passive teaching compared to UCPH. Get ready for a lot of lectures especially if you are in a masters programme.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Numerical probability is a good course. Although high workload. 
I would strongly recommend Mean Field Games in the second semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Paying for girls on dates. This can quickly add up if you hinge profile is on fire. I get the impression that here it is more customary for the guy to pay in the first date:))

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Coffee was cheaper than in Copenhagen. That being said the coffee scene in Copenhagen is exceptionally expensive.
Housing was more expensive than CPH
Going out eating and drinking was in general cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When you arrive you are met with so many offers it is overwhelming. Student associations, sports etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can find something for all interests some examples I were met with: Communist meetings, religious cults, Judo, Climbing, Chess, Soccer, Running and ski trips. You can really find anything in Paris.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Something that interests you? The chess tournament for example looked nice if you are into that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Eiffel tower would be a good starting point.
But I can't list everything so here is a travel guide for starters:
https://heleneinbetween.com/2024/05/essential-paris-travel-guide.html
I really liked the 13th (south), 11th and 6th arrondissements. I also recommend hanging out in Marias (outside of the touristic periods). If you have a little extra time I know people who went outside of Paris to wine tastings or daytrips to other cities (TGV tickets are wayy cheaper outside of national holidays).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy not really something I gave much thought to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Keep trying... It is hard to crack the hard shell of the french but keep going!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That the french people do everything outside of their home. They stay out most of the day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Reflect on what you would like to get out of your exchange before going. For example is it a crazy study load of intense courses or a lot of wild night life experiences?

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you look for housing early on

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Progressing in french and making so many new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Stochastic control in french💀

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
